stem:
Three points $P$, $Q$ and $T$ in three-dimensional space have position vectors
$\mathbf{p} = 3\mathbf{i} - 2\mathbf{j} + \mathbf{k}$, $\quad\mathbf{q} = 7\mathbf{i} + 4\mathbf{j} - \mathbf{k}$ $\quad$ and $\quad\mathbf{t} = a\mathbf{i} + 13\mathbf{j} + b\mathbf{k}$,
where $a$ and $b$ are constants.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the displacement $\overrightarrow{PQ}$ and write it in terms of $\mathbf{i}$, $\mathbf{j}$ and $\mathbf{k}$. (2)

mark_scheme.for: Works out $\mathbf{q} - \mathbf{p}$ one component at a time, i.e. $(7-3)\mathbf{i} + (4-(-2))\mathbf{j} + (-1-1)\mathbf{k}$, with at least two of the three components correct
mark_scheme.notes: Using $\mathbf{p} - \mathbf{q}$ is M0. A column vector is fine.

hints: To go from $P$ to $Q$ you go back to the origin and then out to $Q$, so the vector is $-\mathbf{p} + \mathbf{q}$.
Subtract each component of $\mathbf{p}$ from the matching component of $\mathbf{q}$.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The point $T$ is on the straight line through $P$ and $Q$. Find the value of $a$ and the value of $b$. (3)

mark_scheme.for: Writes down a vector from a known point to $T$ in terms of $a$ and $b$, e.g. $\overrightarrow{PT} = (a-3)\mathbf{i} + 15\mathbf{j} + (b-1)\mathbf{k}$
mark_scheme.notes: Allow a slip in one component. Accept $\overrightarrow{QT} = (a-7)\mathbf{i} + 9\mathbf{j} + (b+1)\mathbf{k}$.

mark_scheme.for: Sets their $\overrightarrow{PT} = \lambda\,\overrightarrow{PQ}$ (their PQ from (a)), gets $\lambda$ from the $\mathbf{j}$ components ($15 = 6\lambda$, so $\lambda = \tfrac{5}{2}$) and uses that $\lambda$ in at least one of the other components
mark_scheme.notes: Depends on the first M1. Also allow the equivalent line equation $\mathbf{r} = \mathbf{p} + \lambda(4\mathbf{i}+6\mathbf{j}-2\mathbf{k})$ with $-2 + 6\lambda = 13$.

alternatives.name: Way 2 (using Q as the fixed point)

marks.for: Sets $\overrightarrow{QT} = \mu(4\mathbf{i}+6\mathbf{j}-2\mathbf{k})$, gets $\mu = \tfrac{3}{2}$ from $9 = 6\mu$ and uses it in another component

solution.working: $T$ lies on line $PQ$, so $\overrightarrow{PT} = \lambda\,\overrightarrow{PQ} = \lambda(4\mathbf{i} + 6\mathbf{j} - 2\mathbf{k})$. The $\mathbf{j}$ components give $15 = 6\lambda$, so $\lambda = \tfrac{5}{2}$. Then $a - 3 = 4\times\tfrac{5}{2} = 10$ and $b - 1 = -2\times\tfrac{5}{2} = -5$.

hints: If $T$ is on the line through $P$ and $Q$, then $\overrightarrow{PT}$ must be a scalar multiple of $\overrightarrow{PQ}$.
The $\mathbf{j}$ component of $\mathbf{t}$ is known, so use it to find the scalar first.

pitfalls.text: If you work out $\mathbf{p} - \mathbf{q}$ you get $-4\mathbf{i} - 6\mathbf{j} + 2\mathbf{k}$. That is $\overrightarrow{QP}$, not $\overrightarrow{PQ}$, so you lose the M1 and the A1. The vector from $P$ to $Q$ is 'end minus start'.
Adding the position vectors instead of subtracting them gives $10\mathbf{i} + 2\mathbf{j} + 0\mathbf{k}$, which does not describe the displacement. This scores no marks.

Take care if you write $\overrightarrow{PT}$ as $\mathbf{p} - \mathbf{t}$ but keep $\overrightarrow{PQ} = \mathbf{q} - \mathbf{p}$. The scalar must then be $\lambda = -\tfrac{5}{2}$. If you drop the sign and use $\tfrac{5}{2}$, you get $a = -7$ and $b = 6$, and the method and accuracy marks are lost. Always use 'end minus start' for both vectors.

The $\mathbf{j}$ component of $\overrightarrow{PT}$ is $13 - (-2) = 15$, not $13 - 2 = 11$. A wrong sign here gives the untidy scalar $\tfrac{11}{6}$ and wrong values of $a$ and $b$, so you lose the A1.

You earn nothing for guessing values of $a$ and $b$ and saying $T$ 'looks' collinear. You need to write $\overrightarrow{PT} = \lambda\,\overrightarrow{PQ}$, find $\lambda = \tfrac{5}{2}$ and use that same $\lambda$ in every component. Without this you do not get the dM1.
